solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Yellow flower for cartoon duck (5)

blocks.note: a colloquial pet name for the daffodil, clipped from its first syllables
the black, lisping duck of Warner Bros' Looney Tunes

annotation.surface: A garden flower chosen as the name for an animated duck.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a naming story, but both halves simply mean DAFFY: the daffodil's pet name and the Looney Tunes duck.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal clipping: the daffodil gets shortened to daffy in casual British speech.

entries.clue: Diamonds on top of elegant dress for ball (8)

indicatorNotes.on top of: in a down answer the earlier letters sit physically on top of the later ones, so D is placed above what follows
indicatorNotes.top of: the top of a word in a down grid is its uppermost, first letter

blocks.note: D = diamonds, the card suit
first letter of elegant
livery = a uniform or distinctive dress

annotation.surface: A jewelled gown chosen for a grand ball.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants a ballgown, but ball is the cricket sense: each ball a bowler sends down is a DELIVERY.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket term: every single ball bowled at the batsman is counted as one delivery.

entries.clue: Country farm on a corner’s fenced off (6)

indicatorNotes.fenced off: a fenced-off area is enclosed on all sides, as the answer is enclosed inside the run of words

blocks.note: farM ON A COrner's

annotation.surface: A rural plot on a corner that has been fenced in.
annotation.walkthrough: The rural picture of farms and fencing is far from the tiny Mediterranean principality it conceals.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Riviera principality is one sovereign state among many.

entries.clue: Listen, perceiving sounds, sensing threat first of all (4)

indicatorNotes.first of all: read as 'the first of all these words': take the opening letter of each one

blocks.note: Perceiving Sounds Sensing Threat

annotation.surface: Someone on alert, ears pricked for danger.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an imperative, the call 'Listen!', and PSST is the hiss that does the same job.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection swap: the whispered hiss for attention stands in for the command 'Listen!'

entries.clue: Holy cow, something I should keep? (2,4)

blocks.note: an exclamation of astonishment, not a sacred animal
a promise I give is something I am bound to keep

annotation.surface: A sacred cow treated as a possession one ought to guard.
annotation.walkthrough: Holy cow reads as a sacred animal but is an exclamation; the question mark flags the playful second definition, keeping one's promise.
annotation.definitionFit: Two interchangeable exclamations of surprise, and separately the promise one gives and keeps.

entries.clue: More than one horned animal with insect runs off (9)

blocks.note: an ant is an insect
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

annotation.surface: Some animal fleeing from a stinging insect.
annotation.walkthrough: The plural in the definition is spelt out ('more than one'), matching the final S.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the definition spells out a plural of hoofed, horned African grazers.

entries.clue: What is wearing coarser knitted jumper, say (9)

indicatorNotes.wearing: whatever wears something has it on the outside, so the rearranged coarser goes around EH
indicatorNotes.knitted: wool that is knitted is worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters, rearranged to RAC…ORSE
eh? = what is it? what did you say?

annotation.surface: A garment question: what is being worn inside a rough knitted sweater.
annotation.walkthrough: Knitted and jumper make a woolly picture, but a jumper here is a horse that jumps fences; 'say' signals the answer is just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a steeplechaser clears fences, so it is one kind of jumper.

entries.clue: Story-telling stretched out? (5)

blocks.note: 'telling stories' in the sense of fibbing
reclining flat at full length

annotation.surface: A tale that has been padded out too long.
annotation.walkthrough: Story-telling is meant in the sense of 'telling stories', fibbing, rather than narrating.
annotation.definitionFit: One word, two verbs: to lie means both to tell untruths and to recline.

entries.clue: Seize knave after good morning (6)

indicatorNotes.after: one thing that comes after another is written later, so knave follows the greeting

blocks.note: hi = a greeting
the knave is the jack in a pack of cards

annotation.surface: A scoundrel grabbing something just after a cheerful greeting.
annotation.walkthrough: Knave is the old name for the jack in playing cards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking over a plane or vehicle by force is seizing it.

entries.clue: Vast land mass in Colombia evacuated after a day (6)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: a building evacuated has its insides emptied, so Colombia loses every letter but its outer two
indicatorNotes.after: one thing that comes after another is written later, so the emptied Colombia follows A FRI

blocks.note: as written
FRI = Friday
first and last letters of Colombia

annotation.surface: A huge region of Colombia cleared of people a day later.
annotation.walkthrough: Colombia tempts a South American answer, but it only supplies its two outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A description of a continent: the definition calls it by what it is, an enormous land mass.

entries.clue: Leotard I designed, made to measure (8)

indicatorNotes.designed: something designed is given a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A dancer boasting of a leotard they designed to fit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all dressmaking, and so is the answer: a rare clue where fodder and definition share a scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from dressmaking: clothes cut to one wearer's measurements.

entries.clue: Woozy choir quaffs English stout (6)

indicatorNotes.Woozy: someone woozy is dizzy and unsteady, so the letters of choir reel into a new order
indicatorNotes.quaffs: to quaff is to drink down, taking something inside, so E goes into the muddled choir

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters, rearranged to H…ROIC
E = English

annotation.surface: A tipsy choir downing English stout, the dark beer.
annotation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the beer the choir is drinking, but it is the adjective meaning brave.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense of the word: stout-hearted means brave, as a hero is.

entries.clue: Strike device with hands (5)

blocks.note: British slang for punching someone
a timepiece with hour and minute hands

annotation.surface: A machine with hands used for punching.
annotation.walkthrough: Strike also suggests a clock chiming the hour, a neat overlap between the two senses.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang verb plus everyday noun: to hit someone, and the timepiece on the wall.

entries.clue: Hand slightly damaged, that hurt to put it mildly! (3,3)

indicatorNotes.slightly damaged: a thing damaged is knocked out of shape, so the four letters of hand are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
ow! = a cry of pain

annotation.surface: Someone nursing a bruised hand, understating how much it stung.
annotation.walkthrough: AND HOW! is an emphatic 'very much so', the reply that says a remark understates things.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases insist that the truth is stronger than the words just used.

entries.clue: Resort reveals it is able to adapt (9)

indicatorNotes.Resort: read as re-sort: to sort again is to put letters into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A holiday resort showing it can change with the times.
annotation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a noun, a holiday destination, but it is a verb: sort again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something versatile turns easily to many uses.

entries.clue: Dismiss retreat with victory, ultimately (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of victory is used

blocks.note: a den is a private retreat
last letter of victory

annotation.surface: A general brushing off a withdrawal that ended in victory.
annotation.walkthrough: Retreat is a noun here, a hideaway, not the military withdrawal the surface implies.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reject a claim or accusation as untrue.

entries.clue: Dump cheap drink (5)

blocks.note: to set something down heavily and carelessly
British slang for cheap, rough wine

annotation.surface: Pouring away some cheap booze.
annotation.walkthrough: The British slang word for rough cheap wine is also the verb for setting something down with a thud.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal verb plus British slang noun: plump down heavily, and cheap wine.

entries.clue: Bird, one cooked after bacon (6)

indicatorNotes.cooked: food that is cooked is transformed, so the letters of one are made into a new order
indicatorNotes.after: one thing that comes after another is written later, so the cooked one follows the bacon

blocks.note: bacon comes from the pig
anagram fodder, 3 letters

annotation.surface: A cook frying a bird after the breakfast bacon.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes cooked look like a recipe step; it is the signal to rearrange one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the pigeon is one bird among many.

entries.clue: Champ in shape after start of competition (4)

indicatorNotes.after: one thing that comes after another is written later, so shape follows C
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of competition
to hew is to shape by cutting

annotation.surface: A champion in good form after a contest begins.
annotation.walkthrough: Champ looks like a champion, but it is the verb for munching noisily.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to champ is to bite and grind noisily, as a horse at the bit.

entries.clue: Snag covered by Tom, perhaps in talk (8)

indicatorNotes.covered by: something covered by another has it wrapped around it, so CAT goes around HITCH

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat; 'perhaps' marks an example
a hitch is a snag or problem

annotation.surface: A problem glossed over by some man called Tom during a discussion.
annotation.walkthrough: Tom reads as a man's name; here it is a tom cat, split around HITCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: idle, casual conversation.

entries.clue: Curious, in the manner of sovereign (6)

blocks.note: as = like, in the manner of
a king is a sovereign

annotation.surface: Behaving oddly, like a monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: Curious here means inquisitive, not strange: someone putting questions.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose adjectival sense: an inquisitive person is forever putting questions.

entries.clue: Reveal rogue craft (6)

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue
art = craft, skill

annotation.surface: Exposing a scoundrel's cunning.
annotation.walkthrough: Craft reads as cunning in the surface but gives ART, craft as skill.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pass on or disclose information.

entries.clue: Backing this country, stand by country (6)

indicatorNotes.Backing: to back is to move backwards, so the letters for this country run in reverse

blocks.note: a British setter's own country is the UK
to stand by is to wait

annotation.surface: A patriotic call to back your own nation and stand by another.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British newspaper 'this country' means the UK. The setter uses country twice on purpose: once in the wordplay, once as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Gulf emirate is one country among many.

entries.clue: Equine sound from mouth of weary hybrid equine (6)

indicatorNotes.mouth of: the mouth of a river or cave is its opening, so take the opening letter of weary

blocks.note: first letter of weary
a hinny is the offspring of a stallion and a female donkey

annotation.surface: A tired mule-like animal letting out a neigh.
annotation.walkthrough: A hinny is the less familiar cousin of the mule: horse father, donkey mother. Equine appears twice on purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the gentle, high neigh a horse makes.

entries.clue: Mixed up, in the drink (2,3)

blocks.note: confused, bewildered
the drink is slang for the sea

annotation.surface: Something stirred into a beverage.
annotation.walkthrough: Mixed up looks like an anagram signal but is the definition: confused.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom plus a literal sense: lost and bewildered, and out on the ocean.

entries.clue: Old copper in standard valve (8)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so O PC goes inside STOCK

blocks.note: stock = standard, as in a stock answer
O = old
a copper is a police constable, PC

annotation.surface: A retired policeman fitting a regulation valve.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal of plumbing pipes, but it is a British policeman.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the tap that shuts off a water supply is one kind of valve.

entries.clue: Charitable donation originally supporting family (4)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter of donation is used
indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down answer a support sits underneath, so D goes below KIN

blocks.note: kin = family
first letter of donation

annotation.surface: A charity gift made to help a family.
annotation.walkthrough: Charitable reads as describing the donation, but it stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: generous and well-disposed towards others.

entries.clue: Kindle being seen when heard (6)

indicatorNotes.when heard: the answer is taken as it strikes the ear, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: in sight = visible, being seen

annotation.surface: A reading device noticed only once it makes a sound.
annotation.walkthrough: Kindle suggests the e-reader, but it is the verb: to stir up feelings.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: to kindle anger or rebellion is to stir it up.

entries.clue: Flash talent on the radio (5)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio carries only sound, so the word is taken as it is heard, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: flair = a natural talent

annotation.surface: A showy performer broadcasting on air.
annotation.walkthrough: Flash reads as flashy talent, but it is the noun: a sudden burst of light.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a sudden bright burst of light or flame.

entries.clue: Yours truly sister saw overwhelmed (9)

blocks.note: yours truly = the speaker, I
a nun is a religious sister
to see someone romantically = to date them

annotation.surface: A speaker confessing their sister saw them swamped.
annotation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past of 'see' meaning notice; it is 'see' as in go out with.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: swamped as if by a flood, with too much to handle.
